Marissa / Kim — put together three viable packaging options. I attached a quick worksheet; the numbers below are rounded for the thread. Full detail in commit-rebate-model.xlsx.

Option A — Annual commit, moderate rebate (12 mo)- Base: 2 standby seats + 3 rotating backups- Failover credits: 10 regional credits / year (72h fastpath each)- Effective unit: $0.018/token-equivalent (blended)- Rebate: 8% at 12 months if commit > $250k TCV

Option B — Multi-year 36-month commit (best unit economics)- Base: 2 standby seats + scale buffer + surge credits for 8-10 weeks- Failover credits: 30 regional credits across term- Effective unit: $0.013/token-equivalent (blended)- Rebate: 14% at renewal tranches; up-front amortization reduces cash outlay

Option C — No-commit monthly (flexible)- Higher per-unit rate, failover credits one-off purchase, no rebates- Effective unit: $0.026/token-equivalent

Notes / constraints: 
- Failover credits are non-refundable but can be moved between legal entities if we add a short inter-entity addendum (needs Legal sign-off).
- For short-term surge (6 FTE for 8 weeks), best economics is to pre-buy a surge block at a discounted rate vs pay-as-you-go. I modeled a 20% discount on surge blocks under Option B.
- If we want to extend an additional 2–5% concession, Finance needs a signed LOI or minimal TCV threshold to greenlight.

Attaching: commit-rebate-model.xlsx (detailed TCV scenarios)

CC: kimberly for any specific on-call scheduling constraints or operational notes.

-karthik
Head of Pricing & Packaging, Redwood Inference

High level: we can meet the peak-month surge with a pre-bought surge block that is significantly cheaper than ad-hoc hourly surcharges; failover credits are non-refundable but transferable between your subsidiaries with a short addendum (Legal will prepare).

Summary (short):
- Option A (12mo, mid rebate): conservative TCV, 10 failover credits, good for teams prioritizing cash flow.
- Option B (36mo, best economics): lowest blended unit, includes surge blocks sized for the 8-week peak and 30 failover credits across the term. Recommended if you can commit to 36 months.
- Option C (no-commit): highest unit cost, flexible, good if you want to avoid long-term commitment.

We can offer an additional 2% one-time discount on Option B if you sign an LOI by 10/10 and agree to an annual reconciliation cadence. That concession requires Finance pre-approval (we have it tentatively for this deal size).
